bHIVE clustering through bluster

Source: R/bHIVEParam.R
bHIVEParam.Rd

Run bHIVE clustering through clusterRows, the bluster interface that bluster::clusterSweep() builds on. This makes bHIVE a drop-in alternative to the k-means, SOM and graph-based clustering that bluster already wraps.

Usage

bHIVEParam(
  nAntibodies = NULL,
  beta = NULL,
  epsilon = NULL,
  maxIter = NULL,
  k = NULL,
  affinityFunc = NULL,
  distFunc = NULL,
  initMethod = NULL,
  scale = NULL,
  targetK = NULL,
  epsilonQuantile = NULL,
  affinityParams = list(),
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'bHIVEParam'
.defaultScalarArguments(x)

# S4 method for class 'bHIVEParam'
show(object)

# S4 method for class 'ANY,bHIVEParam'
clusterRows(x, BLUSPARAM, full = FALSE)

Arguments

nAntibodies, beta, epsilon, maxIter, k, affinityFunc, distFunc, initMethod, scale, targetK, epsilonQuantile

Scalar arguments passed to bHIVE. NULL (the default) uses the bHIVE() default. These can be varied with bluster::clusterSweep().

affinityParams

Named list passed to bHIVE(), for example list(alpha = "auto"). An empty list uses the bHIVE() default.

...

Further named arguments passed to bHIVE() and AINet, such as coverageBoost, consolidate, verbose or immunology modules (shm, idiotypic, ...). Note that R6 modules carry state, so a MemoryPool passed here is shared across every run that uses this parameter object.

x

A numeric matrix-like object with observations in rows, or a bHIVEParam for show().

object

A bHIVEParam object.

BLUSPARAM

A bHIVEParam object.

full

Logical. Return the full bHIVE() result as well as the clusters.

Value

bHIVEParam() returns a bHIVEParam object, a subclass of BlusterParam.

clusterRows() returns a factor of cluster labels, one per row of x. With full = TRUE it returns a list with clusters and objects, where objects$bHIVE is the bHIVE() result, including the fitted AINet model in objects$bHIVE$model for labeling new cells.

Details

bHIVE learns a set of prototypes (antibodies) by clonal selection, mutation and network suppression, then assigns each observation to its nearest prototype. By default the number of clusters emerges from suppression. Set targetK to force exactly that many clusters. For mass cytometry, scale = "arcsinh" and affinityParams = list(alpha = "auto") are good starting points. Progress output is off unless verbose = TRUE is passed through ....

See also

bHIVE, clusterRows, clusterSweep.

Examples

library(bluster)
X <- as.matrix(iris[, 1:4])

p <- bHIVEParam(targetK = 3, maxIter = 10)
p
#> class: bHIVEParam
#> nAntibodies: [default]
#> beta: [default]
#> epsilon: [default]
#> maxIter: 10
#> k: [default]
#> affinityFunc: [default]
#> distFunc: [default]
#> initMethod: [default]
#> scale: [default]
#> targetK: 3
#> epsilonQuantile: [default]
#> affinityParams(0): 
#> extra(0): 
set.seed(1)
clusters <- clusterRows(X, p)
table(clusters, iris$Species)
#>         
#> clusters setosa versicolor virginica
#>        1      0         47        14
#>        2     50          0         0
#>        3      0          3        36

# Full output keeps the fitted model for labeling new cells
out <- clusterRows(X, p, full = TRUE)
out$objects$bHIVE$model$predict(X[1:5, ])
#>      [,1]
#> [1,]    3
#> [2,]    3
#> [3,]    3
#> [4,]    3
#> [5,]    3

# Sweep over parameters
sweep <- clusterSweep(X, bHIVEParam(maxIter = 5), nAntibodies = c(10, 30))
sweep$parameters
#> DataFrame with 2 rows and 1 column
#>                nAntibodies
#>                  <numeric>
#> nAntibodies.10          10
#> nAntibodies.30          30

# Cluster a SingleCellExperiment embedding and store the labels
library(SingleCellExperiment)
sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(logcounts = t(X)))
reducedDim(sce, "PCA") <- prcomp(X)$x[, 1:3]
colLabels(sce) <- clusterRows(reducedDim(sce, "PCA"), p)
table(colLabels(sce), iris$Species)
#>    
#>     setosa versicolor virginica
#>   1      0         48        14
#>   2     50          0         0
#>   3      0          2        36
